static_traits.name: Lin Xueting
static_traits.social_status: Somewhat tense relationships with friends, often declining socializing to save money; has a few friends to confide in, but has not yet talked with them about financial troubles
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never had similar problems before; never received psychotherapy before
static_traits.language_features: Clear and organized expression; able to specifically describe the trigger-emotion-behavior cycle; harsh self-evaluation, leaning negative; Good cooperation, able to accept exploration and exercise suggestions

basic_info.main_problem: I overspend when shopping, then feel strong guilt, and believe I will never be able to save money.
basic_info.core_demands: The recurring 'overspending-guilt' cycle has affected my mental health and financial stability, so I have come to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I cannot trust myself to control spending

special_situations.event: After experiencing stress or a bad day, sees a product she likes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not immediately reward myself, negative emotions are hard to ease; shopping is the only way to feel better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses shopping to regulate emotions and briefly lift mood
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have had enough, I should be good to myself, buying it will make me happy

special_situations.event: After making a budget and sticking to it for days or weeks, temptation or stress appears
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as one slip occurs, it proves I completely failed, unable to self-control
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gives up the budget in a smash-it-all manner and spends impulsively
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed again, I simply cannot do it

special_situations.event: After the most recent shopping spree, checks the bill or recalls spending records
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot manage money as disciplined as others, it shows I am an irresponsible failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blame; avoids going out with friends to reduce spending
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Others all manage well, only I am failing

special_situations.event: Thinking about future financial situation and savings goals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Not controlling spending now means the future will surely be a mess, I will never save money in my lifetime
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My financial future will collapse, I will never save money

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as a disciplined, trustworthy person in control of finances, and to gain affirmation and a sense of security
core_conflict.fear: Fearing loss of control and failure being seen by others as irresponsible, thereby bringing shame, judgment and future insecurity
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control through harsh self-criticism and a strict budget
Avoiding socializing to reduce spending and external judgment

object_relations.self_representation: A person unable to trust one's own impulses, prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others are disciplined and judgmental bystanders ('they are all more organized than me')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to try practicing, reality-testing, or making a change plan
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries about failing again, feels the demands of change are too high and hard to achieve
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First fully Empathize with their worries, tone gentle, concretize goals; using small-step focus, emphasizing trial-and-error experimental language, inviting them to propose the smallest change they can make.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing an overspending experience and the guilt that followed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing failure entirely to oneself, Turning anger and frustration against the self
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reducing judgment, naming shame and guilt, using gentle reflection and Clarification, assisting to distinguish 'behavior and worth', Guiding self-compassion and functional correction.

manifestations: Avoiding going out with friends to save money
Not yet disclosing financial troubles to friends
Feels torn between choice and responsibility: longs for discipline but is pulled by impulses
Worrying about being unable to control future financial stability

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial (such as 'I cannot do it' 'I will always return to old habits')
Skeptical and cautious about trying change
Worrying that everyone else is doing better

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Avoiding going out with friends to save money, Repressing stress inward
Blames oneself harshly when guilty instead of seeking support

exception_events.target_problem: When feeling stressed or seeing products she likes, the client usually consumes impulsively, afterward feels guilt and breaks the savings plan.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the first few days to weeks after making a budget, the client is able to spend according to plan, reduce impulse buying, and reports that guilt is relatively reduced.
exception_events.reason: Cues: because a concrete budget was made in advance and self-monitoring was carried out, and meanwhile stress was relatively low in the short term and the goal was clear enough, better control over impulses appeared.

positive_force: Has experience trying budget and expense tracking, able to persist in the short term and see results
Willing to try new practices and methods, with clear motivation (hoping to break free of the 'overspending - guilt' cycle)
Able to identify trigger situations and automatic thoughts (such as 'I deserve to reward myself')
Has certain social support resources (a few friends to confide in)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing and all-or-nothing Reinforcing helplessness (such as 'I will never save money')
Uses shopping as the main emotion-regulation method, causing short-term relief but long-term rebound
Intense shame and self-blame, tending to attribute failure entirely to oneself
Avoiding socializing to save money, weakening support and worsening Loneliness
Doubts about his own controllability and negative predictions ('destined to fail')

antecedent: Increased stress or experiencing a bad day
The thought 'I deserve to treat myself / buying it will make me happier' appears
A few days into executing the budget, encounters temptation or setbacks
target_behavior.core_reason: Using shopping as the main emotional-regulation means; catastrophizing and all-or-nothing Interpretation of failure intensifying the 'giving up entirely' rebound
target_behavior.function: Gains immediate emotional relief and short-term rewards
target_behavior.consequence: Unable to save steadily, worrying about future finances, accompanied by Strong guilt and self-blame

antecedent: Thinking about guilt and tension from recent spending
Worrying about spending and losing control in social settings
target_behavior.core_reason: To avoid further expenses and being evaluated, contracts the pressure inward rather than seeking external support
target_behavior.function: Escapes potential expenses and the risk of being evaluated by others
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with friends, Increased sense of loneliness, emotionally Decreased support
